title: Central bank policy rates and monetary policy stance
note: Central bank policy rates for the four markets covered by the terminal, read from the central banks themselves on 2026-10-12: the Central Bank of Kenya, the Central Bank of Nigeria, the South African Reserve Bank and the Central Bank of Egypt. Every rate carries the source_url actually fetched and an as-of date. No rate is estimated, interpolated or carried forward; where a figure could not be read from the central bank it is absent and the reason is stated. Nigeria's MPR was reset at the 307th MPC on 22 September 2026; South Africa's policy rate was raised 25 bp to 7.25% effective 25 September 2026; Kenya's CBR has been 8.75% since 10 February 2026; Egypt's corridor has been 19.00/20.00/19.50% since 12 February 2026. Egypt's website returns HTTP 403 to direct requests from this host and was read through a read-only translation proxy of the cbe.org.eg URL; that is flagged on the Egypt block. This is a separate file from macro.json, which holds World Bank inflation and GDP with World Bank indicator codes; policy rates come from central banks and have a different shape (per-country corridors, decision dates and meeting histories), so they are kept in their own file rather than merged into macro.json.

policy_rate.name: Central Bank Rate (CBR)
policy_rate.decision: Hold. The Monetary Policy Committee retained the Central Bank Rate at 8.75 percent at its October 7, 2026 meeting.
policy_rate.stance: Hold; the CBR has been 8.75 percent since the 10 February 2026 meeting.
policy_rate.source_note: CBK news item 'MPC retains the CBR at 8.75 percent' and the CBK 'Key Rates' panel (CBR 8.75% as at 07/10/2026).

repo.name: Repo
repo.source_note: Refreshed from the CBK Central Bank Rates monthly series (latest published month, August 2026). The value previously in this file, 9.25 dated 2025-10-15, was a year old and carried no staleness marker; it stood in for the then Central Bank Rate and is replaced rather than carried forward.

countries.history_note: CBK 'Central Bank Rate' page: the CBR decision table (125 dated points, 2008-08-06 to 2026-10-07). The source table lists some 2026 rows out of chronological order; the file stores them by date. A monthly series carrying the CBR, repo, reverse repo, interbank rate, 91/182/364-day T-bill rates and the cash reserve requirement (1991-07 to 2026-08) is in monthly_rates.

policy_rate.name: Monetary Policy Rate (MPR)
policy_rate.decision: MPC 307th meeting (21-22 September 2026): reset the Monetary Policy Rate at 23.00 per cent (from 26.50 per cent) and recalibrated the Standing Facilities Corridor to +50/-300 basis points around the MPR; retained the Cash Reserve Requirement.
policy_rate.stance: Hold-and-reset. The CBN states the reset and corridor recalibration are an operational realignment to strengthen transmission and reinforce the primacy of the MPR, and expressly not a change in the underlying policy stance; the Committee reaffirmed a data-dependent disinflation stance.
policy_rate.source_note: CBN 'Monetary Policy Decisions' page and MPC Communique No.164 (Ref CBN/MPC/COM/164/307), 22 September 2026. The MPR level change from 26.50 to 23.00 was stated in the communique as a reset; the monthly Money Market Indicators table had not yet published a September 2026 observation (last published month, August 2026, is 26.50).

standing_lending_facility.name: Standing Lending Facility (upper corridor)
standing_lending_facility.derivation: MPR + 50 bp, from the published corridor

standing_deposit_facility.name: Standing Deposit Facility (lower corridor)
standing_deposit_facility.derivation: MPR - 300 bp, from the published corridor

cash_reserve_requirement.name: Cash Reserve Requirement (DMB / Merchant / non-TSA public sector)

decisions.detail: MPR reset to 23.00%; corridor recalibrated to +50/-300 bp; CRR retained (45/16/75).
MPR reduced by 50 bp to 26.50%; corridor +50/-450 bp.

countries.history_note: CBN Money Market Indicators monthly series: the MPR from December 2006, the first month the MPR exists in the series, to August 2026 (237 dated points). Before December 2006 the table records the MPR as 0.00 and carries a separate Minimum Rediscount Rate (MRR) series (13.00-14.00 in 2006), which was the policy rate then; those zero rows are excluded here. The September 2026 reset to 23.00 per cent is a decision date and is held in the decisions list until the CBN publishes the monthly observation.

policy_rate.name: SARB Policy Rate (SPR)
policy_rate.alias: formerly the 'repo rate'; renamed SPR on the move to the surplus framework in 2022
policy_rate.decision: Hike. The MPC raised the policy rate by 25 basis points to 7.25%, effective 25 September. The decision was unanimous.
policy_rate.stance: Tightening. The MPC raised the rate citing upside risks to inflation from a persistent global energy/geopolitical supply shock, services inflation above 3% and longer-run expectations around 4% against the 3% target; the QPM path is broadly stable through the rest of this year.
policy_rate.source_note: SARB 'Statement of the Monetary Policy Committee', 23 September 2026; policy rate value and its 2026-10-09 observation date from the SARB Web API (TimeseriesCode MMRD002A).

countries.facilities_note: Empty on purpose: the SARB publishes no separate standing-facility or corridor rate and the MPC sets the single SPR (see corridor_note), so there is no true standing facility to record here. The four SARB figures previously listed in this block (prime lending rate, SABOR, ZARONIA and the 91-day Treasury bill tender rate) are MARKET rates read from the SARB Web API CurrentMarketRates endpoint, not policy rates or central-bank standing facilities. They have been moved to the market_rates block below, which is labelled as market data.

market_rates.note: MARKET RATES, NOT POLICY RATES. These are published market indicators (a bank lending rate, two overnight benchmarks and a primary-market tender rate) read from the SARB Web API CurrentMarketRates endpoint. They are kept separate from the policy_rate above and from facilities so that a market rate is never presented as a policy rate.

countries.corridor_note: The SARB announcement and the monetary-policy pages do not publish a multi-rate corridor table. Since 2022 the SARB operates a surplus framework in which policy transmission works through a deposit facility rather than a lending facility, and the MPC sets the single SPR. No separate standing-facility or corridor rate was published on the SARB pages fetched, so none is recorded here.
countries.history_note: SARB Web API series MMRD002A (SARB Policy Rate), fetched for 2015-01-01 to 2026-10-12: 3073 daily observations. The history stored here is the 32 distinct rate levels with their effective dates (each is a policy change); the full daily series is available from the same endpoint.

policy_rate.name: CBE key policy rates (overnight deposit / overnight lending corridor)
policy_rate.decision: Hold. The MPC decided to keep its key policy rates unchanged: overnight deposit rate 19.00 percent, overnight lending rate 20.00 percent, and the rate of the main operation 19.50 percent; the discount rate was maintained at 19.50 percent.
policy_rate.stance: Hold. The Committee assessed continued disinflation (headline 14.5 percent and core 14.9 percent in August 2026) with a limited demand-side output gap and described the stance as adequately tight.
policy_rate.source_access: cbe.org.eg returns HTTP 403 to direct requests from this host, so the CBE's own pages were read on 2026-10-12 through a read-only translation proxy of the cbe.org.eg URL (www-cbe-org-eg.translate.goog). The content is the CBE's own page text; the CBE URL is recorded as the source.

countries.history_note: CBE overnight deposit and lending corridor as stated at each MPC meeting: 17 dated points from 2024-03-06 to 2026-09-24, read from the CBE's own MPC press releases for those meetings.
